transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-18 14:00 PST | Duration 52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Kim - Redwood AE; Priya Rao - Redwood SE; Jordan Lee - Redwood CSM; Maya Ortiz - Cedarlane Head of Security; Liam Chen - Cedarlane Platform; Sofia Rivera - Cedarlane IAM; Ethan Park - Cedarlane Compliance

00:00 Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda, we'll run through our SSO SAML setup, SCIM provisioning, then map into RBAC patterns and cover audit and encryption needs. sound good?
00:12 Maya Ortiz: Yep, that works. we have a hard constraint on EU residency for trade logs and our security team wants KMS pairing with customer-managed keys.
00:22 Priya Rao: Noted. we'll highlight the KMS flow and where customer-managed keys come in. also we'll show where audit events are emitted and retention knobs.
00:35 Liam Chen: For context, we use Okta as primary IdP, but we're evaluating Ping for federated partners. we currently provision via SCIM to our HR system, so we want to reuse the same model if possible.
00:48 Alex Kim: Perfect — Okta is common, we have a tested path for Okta and Ping. SCIM mapping is straightforward: you can sync groups to Redwood roles. we'll show recommended attributes.
01:05 Sofia Rivera: Quick Q: how do you represent least-privilege? we want to avoid broad admin scopes being provisioned by default.
:15 Priya Rao: Good question. Our recommended pattern is role-tiering: start with 'read-only' roles for service accounts, then scoped 'app-author' roles for product owners, and separate 'admin' for security ops. provisioning uses group-to-role mapping in SCIM so HR or IdP controls membership.
02:02 Jordan Lee: i'll note that for the rollout playbook.
02:10 Ethan Park: on audit logs — what's the granularity and can we ship them to our SIEM? we need immutable logs for compliance.
02:23 Priya Rao: You can configure event sinks to forward audit events over syslog or S3 with server-side immutability. events include token issuance, user-role changes, model invocation summaries (not full request bodies by default), and admin actions. retention can be set per-tenant; EU workloads can retain logs within eu- bucket.
02:45 Maya Ortiz: are the invocation logs PII-free? we can't store raw prompt text in EU storage.
02:53 Alex Kim: By default, hosted logs redact prompt text for sensitive regions; for private deployments you can control retention and masking policies. we'll surface the config keys.
03:10 Liam Chen: on SCIM specifics, what attributes do you expect? groupName, members, externalId?
03:17 Priya Rao: Typical attributes: userName, externalId, emails, displayName, groups. For role mapping we recommend using a group attribute like 'redwoodRole' or map groups via an explicit mapping table. we'll share a template.
03:40 Sofia Rivera: about provisioning speed — we have large org churn. SCIM incremental syncs need to be efficient. any rate limits?
03:49 Priya Rao: Our SCIM endpoint supports incremental delta syncs and we recommend batching changes. There's a throttle at the control plane level to protect runtime — we'll share recommended backoff settings.
04:05 Alex Kim: let's talk SAML: SP metadata, ACS url, and attributes. we support email, name, and a custom 'roles' attribute if your IdP can emit it.
04:20 Liam Chen: we can emit roles as a claim. do you support signature verification with certificate rotation?
04:28 Priya Rao: yes, we support multiple certs in the metadata and JWK URIs for rotation. we also support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows.
04:45 Maya Ortiz: Regarding least-privilege, can we set per-route permissions? e.g., only team A can call certain model endpoints?
04:55 Priya Rao: Yes, RBAC is hierarchical: org -> project -> route. you can attach role policies at each level. policies are declarative and we support attribute-based checks (e.g., group==trading-team && env==prod).
05:18 Ethan Park: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in both hosted and private?
05:24 Alex Kim: In hosted we support BYOK via KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google CMEK) with envelope encryption. For private deployments you can point to an HSM or on-prem KMS. key rotation is supported, and we log key usage in the audit trail.
05:40 Maya Ortiz: How about SOC2 evidence for SSO and key management? we need a mapping of controls.
05:47 Jordan Lee: we'll attach the SOC2 pack and a mapping doc. we also have ISO artifacts. I'll follow up in the email with the control IDs that map to SSO/SCIM/KMS.
06:05 Liam Chen: Any gotchas with SP metadata? our IdP team often uses a different entityID than the expected pattern.
06:12 Alex Kim: We accept arbitrary entityIDs but ACS URL must match. if the IdP does signed assertions with non-standard NameID formats we'll walk through claim mapping.
06:25 Sofia Rivera: Testing plan — how do you recommend validating role mapping end-to-end?
06:30 Priya Rao: Typical workflow: 1) Create test IdP & test user in Okta; 2) Exchange metadata and set up a SCIM service account; 3) Provision a group mapped to a low-priv role; 4) Attempt model invocation for that role and verify permissions and audit logs. We usually run that in a 90 minute workshop.
06:58 Maya Ortiz: We want automation for de-provisioning when employees leave. can SCIM push a 'suspended' state or just remove group membership?
07:08 Priya Rao: SCIM supports 'active' toggle; you can set user.active=false to suspend. We also recommend a periodic reconciliation job if you have high churn.
07:22 Liam Chen: Does Redwood support SCIM bulk import for initial sync?
07:27 Priya Rao: Yes, bulk ops are supported — large CSV or SCIM bulk endpoints. We'll advise a throttled sync to seed roles.
07:36 Alex Kim: quick live demo idea — priya, want to show the mapping UI and audit logs?
07:41 Priya Rao: Yep, i have a small demo. i'll share my screen — apologies if the resolution is weird.
08:00 [screen share noise / brief silence]
08:12 Priya Rao: showing SAML config page: you can upload metadata or paste IdP xml. here's where you drop in the ACS and audience. here's the attribute mapping panel where you can map SAML claims to Redwood attributes like 'email' and 'redwood_role'.
08:45 Sofia Rivera: can we namespace roles to avoid collision across teams?
08:50 Priya Rao: we support namespacing, e.g., 'trading:reader' vs 'ops:admin'. recommended practice is prefixing teams.
09:12 Maya Ortiz: audit event example?
09:15 Priya Rao: example event: {event: 'role.assign', actor: 'admin@cedarlane.com', target: 'user:bob', role: 'trading:writer', ts: '2026-01-18T14:09:43Z'}. Note: in hosted EU we strip prompt content by default.
09:40 Liam Chen: can we forward those records to our Splunk instance?
09:45 Priya Rao: yes via S3 forwarder or webhook to your collector; we can do structured JSON lines for easier ingestion.
10:02 Ethan Park: about encryption at rest — what's the default? AES-256? any FIPS mode?
10:10 Alex Kim: default is AES-256-GCM; for FIPS we have options in private deployments and CMK support with HSM-backed providers for FIPS compliant stacks.
10:26 Maya Ortiz: we need proof of key separation — that Redwood operations can't decrypt customer payloads.
10:33 Jordan Lee: for BYOK we provide a technical note showing envelope encryption and how keys are never persisted unwrapped. we'll include that in the follow-up.
10:45 Liam Chen: data residency: we have EU trading desks. how do we ensure models and logs stay in eu- region?
10:53 Priya Rao: You can pin a project to a region. compute and logs will be placed in the configured region. for hosted we offer eu-central region for EU residency. cross-region replication is opt-in.
11:10 Sofia Rivera: regulatory question: do you support export controls or data exfil protections for prompts?
11:18 Priya Rao: We offer prompt redaction and allow customers to disable certain telemetry. For regulated use we recommend private deployment or strict retention policies.
11:35 Maya Ortiz: timeline & gating: our security committee needs SAML proof of concept and a SOC2 mapping before procurement can sign.
11:42 Alex Kim: understood. proposed timeline: metadata exchange this week, provisioning smoke test next week, SOC2 artifacts in parallel.
11:50 Ethan Park: any licensing or dedicated capacity talks we should consider? if we pin for EU we may want dedicated capacity for latency and isolation.
11:58 Alex Kim: yes — Dedicated gives reserved pools and stronger SLA. we can price a pilot for you.
12:10 Liam Chen: what about emergency access and break glass for ops? can we have an audited emergency flow?
12:17 Priya Rao: yes — emergency accounts are time-limited and require multi-party approval; we log every step and emit an audit entry.
12:30 Maya Ortiz: outstanding questions: 1) provide sample SP metadata 2) show SCIM mapping template 3) confirm log retention defaults for eu workloads 4) KMS integration technical note
12:44 Alex Kim: we'll send all four. Jordan will attach SOC2/ISO artifacts. Priya will lead the provisioning workshop.
12:55 Jordan Lee: i'll schedule the workshop and include an invite for the IdP team and your platform engineer.
13:05 Maya Ortiz: thanks — that's helpful. looking forward to the workshop.
13:12 Alex Kim: thanks all. we'll follow up with the checklist and next steps by EOD.
13:18 [meeting ended]

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and small phrase substitutions (e.g., 'redwoodRole' might appear as 'redwood role') are present.
